Rumored for some time, Apple has been developing an all-glass new design to mark the twentieth anniversary of the iPhone next year. However, analysts at Jefferies believe the device has already been shelved.

Wall Street analysts say the major iPhone redesign planned for the twentieth anniversary has been cancelled.

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee (李裕生) citing the likely cancellation of the twentieth-anniversary iPhone redesign as the main reason.

The key to this downgrade is the suspected cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although reports as early as 2025 indicated the project was under development, and rumours suggested a launch as soon as 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent application for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies previously considered an all-glass iPhone launch reasonable, but Edison Lee believes development work has stalled. The analyst pointed out that supply chain checks show the project was cancelled due to overly low yield rates. Edison Lee considers this decision "a major setback to efforts to push for higher-priced iPhones at a time when memory costs are soaring." If the device were indeed launched in September 2027 to mark the iPhone's twentieth anniversary, the estimated average retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Edison Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further raising average selling prices and gross margins." He sees this as having been a crucial defensive move against the backdrop of rising memory prices.

Edison Lee also pointed out that Apple's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are additional reasons for further downgrading the company's stock rating.

It is unclear from Edison Lee's report whether he believes the entire redesign has been shelved, or only certain elements have been cancelled.

bcom77's comment received the most likes

It's quite possible that at some point in the not-so-distant future, product pricing will become absurdly expensive, leading consumers to simply stop buying new things. Unless major tech companies seriously address component costs, profit margins will shrink dramatically. They cannot keep passing costs on to consumers indefinitely.

For example, many doubt Apple will be able to fully remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year, making an "all-glass" screen difficult to achieve. But a rumoured four-sided curved design may still be launched.

In any case, if Apple's twentieth-anniversary iPhone redesign has indeed been cancelled, other authoritative sources should confirm it soon.
